title: Machine-learning ink detection lets contestants read sealed Herculaneum scrolls

items.title_found: Vesuvius Challenge 2023 Grand Prize awarded: we can read the scrolls!
items.meta_description: The 2000-year-old scroll discusses music, food, and how to enjoy life’s pleasures.
passages: For this we primarily use a tool called Volume Cartographer, created by Seth Parker and others in Brent Seales’ lab, and augmented by our contestants, primarily Julian Schilliger (Grand Prize winner) and Philip Allgaier.
Vesuvius Challenge 2023 Grand Prize awarded: we can read the first scroll!
February 5th, 2024 We’re announcing the winners of the Vesuvius Challenge 2023 Grand Prize.
On March 15th, 2023, Nat Friedman, Daniel Gross, and Brent Seales launched the Vesuvius Challenge to answer this question.
The results of this review were clear and unanimous: the Vesuvius Challenge Grand Prize of $700,000 is awarded to a team of three for their excellent submission.
Youssef NaderLuke FarritorJulian Schilliger All three winning team members have been strong community contributors since the very beginning of Vesuvius Challenge.

items.meta_description: Vesuvius Challenge uses machine learning and computer vision to read the carbonized Herculaneum scrolls buried by Vesuvius in 79 AD. Over $2,199,250 awarded.
